in_hebrew.name: אפריקה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: God created man in his own image; in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them. And God blessed them, and God said to them, 'Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; and have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over every living thing that moves on the earth.' And man went out from the presence of God to work the ground from which the LORD God had taken this man to make him live. This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day when God created man, he made him in the likeness of God. And he created them male and female and blessed them and named them Man and his wife's name was Woman, when they were naked and not ashamed. Therefore a name of great glory was given to Africa, 'dust,' representing the earthly nature of man, and 'God created' signifying the divine origin of man.

in_greek.name: Αφρίκη
in_greek.long_meaning: The name Africa comes from the Greek word 'Aphríkē,' which means 'dust.' It is believed to have originated from the ancient Greeks' observation of the vast amount of dust and sand that could be seen rising from the African continent when the wind blew over the desert regions.

in_latin.name: Afríca
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name for Africa, 'Afríca,' also comes from the same root as the Greek name. It means 'dust' or 'dry,' reflecting the arid desert conditions that were once prevalent in many parts of the continent.
